narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Engineering Notebook"**

The site is a well-kept engineering pad. Every entry is dated in the left margin, the way a working log is kept, and the writing sits on one narrow ruled column beside it. What is on the record is drawn in technical pen; what Chin still has to confirm is drawn in pencil and left visibly open. Instruments are clipped onto the pages rather than built into them: an index card for navigation (⌘K), a white-pen sketch of the system on a blueprint sheet, a technical drawing with lettered parts for a Case Study, a small print of Chin himself, and link previews pasted in like clippings.

The mood is precise, honest and unhurried. Type does most of the work, and one colour carries the brand: blueprint ultramarine, used as ink for links and the primary action and as a full sheet twice, for the system sketch that opens the page and the Contact block that closes it. The page holds still: motion only settles the first view once and answers what the visitor does. Density is low on purpose: one idea per entry, generous gaps between sections, and the margin dates carrying the structure so headings can stay small.

Honesty is a visual rule here, not just a content rule. A missing fact is drawn as an open item (an unchecked box with "Chin to write" or "Chin to confirm"), never smoothed over with filler.
keyCharacteristics: One 640px measure with a 168px date margin; everything hangs off that sheet.
Light first (engineering pad); dark is the same notebook at night, never a different world.
One brand colour: blueprint ultramarine `#1E34B4`, as pen ink (links, the primary action, drawing strokes) and as two blueprint sheets on home (the sketch and Contact).
Pen (solid) means on the record; pencil (dashed, graphite) means draft.
Mono only where an engineer would write mono: margin dates, figures, code, drawing labels.
Flat pages; only clipped-on objects lift.

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: Blueprint ultramarine is the only chromatic colour on the page, as ink or as a sheet. If something else wants colour, it gets ink weight instead.

rules.name: The Two Sheets Rule
rules.body: The blueprint surface appears twice on home and nowhere else: the opening sketch and the closing Contact block, so the page starts and ends on the brand colour. A third blue region dilutes both.

rules.name: The Pen and Pencil Rule
rules.body: Solid pen blue marks a fact that is on the record; dashed pencil graphite marks a draft for Chin to confirm. Never use pencil for decoration or pen for a guess.

rules.name: The Same Notebook at Night Rule
rules.body: Dark mode swaps every value for its `-dark` twin and changes nothing else: same layout, same rules, same single accent.

rules.name: The Logbook Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono appears only for margin dates, figures, code and drawing part letters. Labels, nav, buttons and tags are always the body face.

rules.name: The Quiet Heading Rule
rules.body: Section heads stay at Headline size against a Hero headline three times their size. Hierarchy comes from that jump, the margin and the gaps, not from shouting.

rules.name: The Margin Carries It Rule
rules.body: If a piece of content has a date, a number or a sequence, that marker goes in the margin. Nothing else does.

rules.name: The Clipped-On Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this object sits on top of the notebook." If it is part of the page, it gets a border, not a shadow.

dos: hang every date, number or sequence marker in the 168px margin, in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures, including how long a role lasted (LinkedIn-style "2 yrs 7 mos", both months counted).
keep one filled pen-blue primary button per screen; everything else is outline or a link.
draw unconfirmed facts in dashed pencil graphite and label them "Chin to confirm".
show missing content as an Open Item with an empty checkbox.
animate only `transform` and `opacity`, under 300ms for UI (enter ease-out, exit faster), with a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback for everything.

keep hover effects inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and every target at 44px; an inline link grows its hit area vertically (padding of `(44px - 1.15em) / 2`, cancelled by a negative margin) so the line never moves.
use a project's own og:image for its preview, and only screenshots of public pages.
donts: introduce a second accent colour, gradients or tinted section backgrounds.
use mono for labels, nav, buttons or tags.
put a shadow on anything that is part of the page; only clipped-on objects lift.
use pills, large radii (the round portrait is the only exception), card grids of identical rounded boxes, or cards inside cards.
add eyebrow labels, tracked capitals, middle-dot meta strings or arrows glued to link text.
invent a number, quote, logo, latency figure or architecture detail to fill a gap.
make dark mode a different design; it is the same notebook at night.
